.. py:function:: nearest_dist_to_vessel_names(vessel_names: List[str], pt_mm: numpy.ndarray, multilabel: numpy.ndarray, spacing, mapping: dict) -> float

   Distance (mm) from *pt_mm* to the nearest voxel of any label named in *vessel_names*.


.. py:function:: anatomical_endpoint_score(pt_mm: numpy.ndarray, rule: Optional[str], axes: Optional[nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy_axes.AnatomicalAxes] = None) -> float

   Ranking score for *pt_mm* under an anatomical direction *rule* (lower = more extreme in that direction).

   With *axes* the rule is resolved against the volume's real orientation and
   the subject's species (see :mod:`nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy_axes`).
   Without it the legacy hardcoded axes are used: array axis 2 = S/I, axis 1 =
   A/P, axis 0 increasing toward L — i.e. an implicit LAS volume.


.. py:function:: anatomical_endpoint_scores(pts_mm: numpy.ndarray, rule: Optional[str], axes: Optional[nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy_axes.AnatomicalAxes] = None) -> numpy.ndarray

   Vectorised :func:`anatomical_endpoint_score` (needed to normalise combined ``a+b`` rules).


.. py:function:: choose_root_endpoint(tree: nvitk.measure.morpho.models.SkeletonTree, vessel_info: nvitk.measure.morpho.models.VesselInfo, multilabel: numpy.ndarray, spacing, mapping: dict, mask_bool: Optional[numpy.ndarray] = None, axes: Optional[nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy_axes.AnatomicalAxes] = None) -> int

   Choose proximal/root endpoint among all skeleton terminals.


.. py:function:: orient_centerline_points_by_flow(pts: numpy.ndarray, vessel_info: nvitk.measure.morpho.models.VesselInfo, multilabel: numpy.ndarray, spacing, mapping: dict, axes: Optional[nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy_axes.AnatomicalAxes] = None) -> Tuple[numpy.ndarray, bool]

   Orient a centerline so it runs upstream→downstream per *vessel_info* flow topology.

   Returns ``(points, was_reversed)``. Falls back through downstream-only, then
   upstream-only proximity when one side of the topology is unavailable, and
   finally onto the vessel's ``no_upstream_start`` anatomical rule. That last
   fallback matters for root vessels whose topology has no usable
   ``flow_from``/``flow_to`` (``"systemic"`` upstream, empty downstream) — e.g.
   every entry in ``mouse_root_topology.json`` — which otherwise get no
   orientation at all when the component is unbranched.


.. py:function:: make_path_id(label: int, vessel_name: str, component_id: int, path_i: int, terminal_i: int, tree_label: Optional[str] = None) -> str

   Build the export filename stem for one centerline path (trunk/arm/anatomic-M1 naming).


.. py:function:: display_anatomic_segment_path(segment_path: str) -> str

   Strip a redundant leading ``M1_`` prefix from a segment path for display.


.. py:function:: make_loop_region_path_id(label: int, vessel_name: str, component_id: int, loop_i: int, region_name: str, region_i: int = 1) -> str

   Build the export filename stem for a donut-loop region (selected/alternate arm).


.. py:function:: make_tree_region_id(label: int, vessel_name: str, component_id: int, role: str) -> str

   Build the export filename stem for a recursive tree-region segment.
